data.title: Fluorescent protein ticker tape (FPTT): Multiplexed recording of transcriptional dynamics in living cells and in vivo
data.authors: Wang R; Jiang J et al.

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.model_system: HEK293T cells, synchronised (live recording of mTOR-driven transcription, SREBP1 response element)
data.finding: Engineered a multiplexed fluorescent-protein 'ticker tape' biosensor platform (self-assembling protein fibers + multispectral fluorescent proteins) for longitudinal, single-cell recording of signaling-pathway transcriptional histories (mTOR, NF-κB, STAT3, NFAT, cAMP). Applying the mTOR-FPTT reporter, the authors independently observed cell-cycle-dependent OSCILLATING mTOR activity dynamics -- a new, orthogonal tool corroborating that mTOR signaling is patterned over time rather than static, consistent with JOS2024's cell-cycle oscillation finding.
data.abstract_excerpt: Recording and real-time imaging of promoter activities are critical for deciphering signaling cross-talk, but technologies for simultaneously capturing multiple transient events in living cells are lacking. Here, we design fluorescent protein-based ticker tapes (FPTT) for multiplexed, scalable, longitudinal recording of single-cell physiological activities by integrating multispectral monomeric fluorescent proteins with self-assembling protein fibers. FPTT logged dose-dependent, reversible endogenous cFos transcriptional histories in hippocampal neurons at 3-hour resolution over 8 days.

extracted_findings.intervention: None (tool development: fluorescent protein ticker-tape reporters)
extracted_findings.target: mTOR-responsive transcription (and NF-kB, STAT3, NFAT, cAMP) recorded over time
extracted_findings.species: HEK293T cells; mouse neurons and liver
extracted_findings.effect: mTOR reporter activity oscillates with the cell cycle in single cells.
